Development of Deuteroalkylthiolating Reagents for Synthesis of Deuterated Sulfides
item.description:
Abstract
Here, we report the synthesis and applications of S-(alkyl-d2) sulfonothioates as deuteroalkylthiolating reagents from easily accessible deuteroalkyl thianthrenium triflates. Notably, these reagents serve as the electrophile or radical acceptor toward reacting with a variety of substrates, including aryl(hetero)boronic acids, terminal alkynes, redox NHPI esters, β-ketoester, and oxindole. Moreover, late-stage modification of bioactive molecules has been conducted.

item.title: Photocatalytic 1,4-Alkylation/Carboxylation of 1,3-Enynes with 4-Alkyl-Hantzsch Esters and CO 2 for the Synthesis of 2,3-Allenoic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, a visible-light-promoted protocol for the regioselective 1,4-alkylation/carboxylation of 1,3-enynes with 4-alkyl-Hantzsch esters and CO2 is described. This approach enabled direct access to a diverse range of tetrasubstituted 2,3-allenoic acids in satisfactory yields. This transformation relies on readily available 4-alkyl-1,4-dihydropyridines as competent alkyl radical precursors, exhibits good functional group tolerance, and is amenable to 1 mmol scale synthesis. The utility of this method is further highlighted by the derivatization of the obtained allenoic acid products.

item.title: Reductive Catalyst Regeneration Enables the General Cu-Catalyzed Atom Transfer Radical Addition with Primary Alkyl Halides
item.description:
Abstract
Primary alkyl halides are poor coupling partners in most atom transfer radical addition (ATRA) reactions due to their propensity to undergo off-cycle radical termination pathways, which lead to catalyst deactivation. Herein, we overcome this challenge in the Cu-catalyzed ATRA reaction though the addition of 1,1′-azobis(cyclohexanecarbonitrile), an in situ reducing agent. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst turnover is restored and challenging halides become competent coupling partners across a variety of substituted alkenes. This strategy enables the synthesis of a diverse array of biologically relevant synthetic intermediates, including α-haloboronic esters, sulfones, esters, amides, and arenes. The versatility and synthetic utility of these ATRA conditions are demonstrated in 48 examples and 13 subsequent functionalizations.

item.title: Biocatalytic Synthesis of Substituted Cinnamaldehydes
item.description:
Abstract
Substituted cinnamaldehydes are valuable compounds, but current syntheses rely on expensive and toxic reagents. We report a biocatalytic synthesis of substituted cinnamaldehydes from the corresponding benzaldehydes via an aldolase, NahE, and benzoylformate decarboxylase. This is the first use of α,β-unsaturated 2-oxo acids as substrates for thiamine diphosphate-dependent 2-oxo acid decarboxylases. We found electron-donating substituents were better tolerated than electron-withdrawing substituents, but all showed good to excellent conversions. A preparative-scale reaction gave 4-methoxycinnamaldehyde in 77% isolated yield.

item.title: Arylcarboxylation/Cyclization/Hydrogenation Cascade of Arylalkynes with Formate: Synthesis of Ester-Substituted Dioxodihydrodibenzothiazepine Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
A novel method has been developed for the arylcarboxylation/cyclization/hydrogenation cascade reaction of arylalkynes with cheap and readily available sodium formate (HCO2Na). This approach facilitates the efficient synthesis of ester-substituted dioxodihydrodibenzothiazepine derivatives in the absence of photocatalysts and transition metals. The methodology features a broad substrate scope, operational simplicity, excellent functional group tolerance, mild reaction conditions, and scalability. Mechanistic experiments proved that the reaction involves a pathway that includes the formation of the carbon dioxide radical anion (CO2•–) from formate. Meanwhile, the hydrogen in the product comes from trace amounts of water in the solvent or HCO2Na.

item.title: Biomimetic Base-Exchange Reaction for Late-Stage Synthesis of Stereodivergent NAADP + and NAD(P) + Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
Nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP+) and related NAD(P)+ analogues are important tools for calcium signaling, redox biology, and chemical biology. Their preparation, however, remains constrained by lengthy dinucleotide synthesis and enzyme-dependent base exchange. Here we describe a biomimetic chemical base-exchange reaction that converts native NAD+ or NADP+ directly into NAAD+, NAADP+, and modified pyridine nucleotide analogues. Fe(III) promotes substitution of the nicotinamide unit through synergistic activation of the cationic C–N glycosidic bond.

item.title: Direct C6-Alkynylation of Indoles by Palladium/Norbornene Cooperative Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
C6–H alkynylation of indoles is a highly attractive yet challenging transformation Herein we report a palladium/norbornene cooperative catalysis strategy that enables direct and regioselective C6–H alkynylation of indoles. The method exhibits broad substrate generality, accommodating a wide range of functional groups, fused heterocycles, and complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that neither C–H cleavage step is turnover-limiting and that both the palladium catalyst and ethynyl benziodoxolone participate in the turnover-limiting step.

item.title: Nondirected Palladium-Catalyzed C(sp 3 )–H Oxygenation with H 2 O 2
item.description:
Abstract
Palladium(II) complexes of the TPA family (TPA = tris(2-pyridylmethyl)amine) catalyze selective C(sp3)–H oxyfunctionalizations but have so far been unable to activate “green” oxidant H2O2, instead requiring peroxycarboxylic acids (2–4 equiv, best results coming with m-CPBA). Herein, we show that hydrogen peroxide itself, conveniently delivered as its solid surrogates (UHP and SPC), can serve as the terminal oxidant in Pd(TPA)-catalyzed nondirected C(sp3)–H oxygenation, with carboxylic acid anhydrides as cocatalytic H2O2 activators. Depending on the conditions, alcohols or ketones form, with the catalyst sustaining up to 1.6 × 104 turnovers. The protocol is applied to the selective oxidation of complex natural products (steroids and terpenoids).

item.title: Functionalization of Polyamide Cages through Peripheral Postmodification
item.description:
Abstract
Polyamide cages are promising receptors in molecular recognition and are potential building blocks of functional materials. Herein, we present a general method to functionalize polyamide cages through peripheral postmodification of brominated polyamide cages, which themselves were able to be synthesized highly efficiently from imine cage precursors through Pinnick oxidation. Suzuki cross-coupling of these brominated cages with aryl boronic acids/esters successfully produced a series of polyamide cages equipped with functional groups, such as hydroxyl, amino, carboxyl, cyano, aldehyde, alkenyl, and solubilizing groups.

item.title: Photoredox-Catalyzed Radical Heterocyclization of Heteroatom-Tethered Alkenes with α-Iodonium Diazo Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
A photoredox-catalyzed radical heterocyclization of alkenoic acids and sulfonamides with α-iodonium diazo compounds is reported. The reaction delivers diazomethyl-containing lactones and pyrrolidines in good yields with full retention of the diazo group. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by a gram-scale synthesis and downstream derivatizations under mild, redox-neutral conditions. A plausible radical–polar crossover mechanism is proposed for this transformation.

item.title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed C–H Activation/[3 + 2] Cycloaddition for the Synthesis of Functionalized Pyrrolo[1,2- a ]imidazole Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
We report a Rh(III)-catalyzed C–H activation/[3 + 2] cycloaddition of heterocyclic ketene aminals (HKAs) 1 with 2,3-diaryl-2H-azirines 2, affording functionalized pyrrolo[1,2-a]imidazoles 3 in moderate to excellent yields. The native nitrogen atom of HKAs serves as an intrinsic directing group, enabling selective α-C–H activation without prior substrate functionalization. The azirines act as unusual C2 synthons, enabling a distinct and highly regioselective [3 + 2] annulation mode complementary to those of alkynes and alkenes. The reaction proceeds under [Cp*RhCl2]2/AgBF4/HOAc catalysis in refluxing acetonitrile under air and exhibits broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic studies support exclusive α-C–H activation and a plausible Rh(III)-catalyzed pathway. This method provides a practical, atom- and step-economical route to structurally diverse pyrrolo[1,2-a]imidazoles.

item.title: A Modular Rapid-Injection NMR for Structure Elucidation and Kinetic Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Rapid-injection nuclear magnetic resonance (RI-NMR) spectroscopy transforms a standard NMR tube into a reaction vessel within the NMR spectrometer, enabling kinetic and spectroscopic characterization of intermediates under synthetically relevant conditions. Despite its versatility as a tool for mechanistic analysis, the broad adoption of RI-NMR has been hindered by the lack of cost- and space-efficient instrument designs, which can be operated with negligible interference to the NMR facility. Herein, we describe an RI apparatus that is compatible with most NMR spectrometers, requires no modification of the NMR instrument or probe, and may be easily transported to and from the laboratory. Accurate reagent delivery is achieved across a range of solvents and temperatures, and samples can be mixed within seconds after injection. The utility of this apparatus is highlighted through four case studies chosen to illustrate different aspects of the instrument.

item.title: Cofixation of NH 3 and CO 2 through Cyclic Diarylchloronium Salt-Triggered Ring-Opening Bifunctionalization of Unstrained Cyclic Amines
item.description:
Abstract
We report a mild and general strategy for the cofixation of NH3 and CO2 via cyclic diarylchloronium salt-triggered ring-opening bifunctionalization of unstrained cyclic amines. This method employs readily available aqueous NH3 and CO2 as nitrogen and carbon feedstocks, delivering valuable carbamates bearing free amino groups (−NH2) in high yields with regiospecificity. Notably, this methodology enables the use of dilute CO2 for the construction of functionalized carbamates, highlighting its potential for waste gas valorization.

item.title: 1,2- seco -Bicyclic Polyprenylated Acylphloroglucinols as Isoform Selective Inhibitors of T-Type Calcium Channels
item.description:
Abstract
Hyreptaones A–E (1–5, respectively), five undescribed 1,2-seco-bicyclic polyprenylated acylphloroglucinols (BPAPs), were discovered in Hypericum reptans. 1–3 constitute the first 1,2-seco-BPAPs originating from rare 3,3-diisoprenylated BPAPs. 4 and 5 possess a spirocyclic 6/5/5 scaffold arising from further cyclization of 1,2-seco-BPAP. Their structures were determined by spectroscopic analysis and X-ray crystallography. 1–5 preferentially inhibited Cav3.1 over other T-type calcium channels, whereas 4 and 5 exhibited state-dependent gating modulation of Cav3.1 and represent a novel class of Cav3.1 allosteric modulators.

item.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Macrocyclic Iminoisocoumarins by Rh-Catalyzed Intramolecular Vinylic C–H Activation/Heterocyclization
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a new macrocyclization strategy via electrochemical Rh(III)-catalyzed intramolecular vinylic C–H activation and subsequent heterocyclization. This approach affords diverse iminoisocoumarin-braced macrocycles with 13- to 28-membered rings bearing various functional groups in good yields with excellent regioselectivity under mild electrooxidation conditions. Mechanistic studies, including isolation and characterization of a key Rh(I) sandwich intermediate, along with cyclic voltammetry analysis, provide evidence for a rhodium(III/I) catalytic regime.

item.title: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butane Carboxamides to N-Heterocycles via a Strain Release-Enabled Nickel(II)–Carbene Intermediate
item.description:
Abstract
We report the conversion of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane carboxamides into N-heterocycles via strain release, enabling the generation of a novel class of Ni(II)–carbene intermediate and utilizing it for Ni(II)–carbene alkyne metathesis reactions for cyclopropanation and [4+2] cycloaddition to access highly functionalized cyclopropane-containing tetracyclic quinolinones and phenanthridinones. This transformation exhibits a broad scope and high yields across diverse substrates, with mechanistic studies confirming the formation of Ni(II)–carbene via a trapping experiment. Synthetic utility was demonstrated, and bioactive molecules were incorporated into the N-heterocyclic core.

item.title: Discovery of Three Macrocyclic Diterpenoid Skeletons from Croton laevigatus and Their NF-κB Inhibitory Activity
item.description:
Abstract
Phytochemical investigation of Croton laevigatus yielded six macrocyclic diterpenoids, craeviganoids A–F (1–6), featuring three novel carbon skeletons: two distinct types of 13-membered diterpenoid lactones (1–3) bearing a rare bridgehead alkene, and a 14-membered furanoditerpenoid skeleton (4–6). Their structures were elucidated by spectroscopic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and quantum chemical calculations, revealing distinct solid-state and solution conformations for 1. Moreover, compound 4 potently inhibited NF-κB and exhibited anti-inflammatory activity.

item.title: γ-Selective Deuteration of Unactivated C(sp 3 )–H Bonds of Aliphatic Amines via Pd Catalysis in D 2 O
item.description:
Abstract
Selective γ-deuteration of unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds in aliphatic amines is achieved using D2O as the sole deuterium source via Pd catalysis with 3-formyl-2-pyridone as a transient directing group. The reaction proceeds in aqueous medium without acidic or fluorinated co-solvents. Branched and cyclic amines are deuterated regioselectively at γ-methyl sites (up to 89% D). The utility is demonstrated by concise synthesis of deuterated scaffolds (rimantadine, ethambutol, and dobutamine) otherwise inaccessible by conventional methods, together with a one-pot γ-deuteration/γ-arylation sequence. Mechanistic studies establish that the pyridone moiety dominates the CMD step and intrinsically favors H/D exchange.

item.title: Uracil-Thianthrenium Salts (Uracil-TT + BF 4 – ) as a Coupling Partner in Sonogashira Cross-Coupling Reactions: Access to 5-Alkynyl Uracils and Synthetic Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Cross-coupling reactions are powerful tools for forging two different organic fragments via formation of C–C or C–heteroatom bonds. Herein, we for the first time synthesize a bench-stable cross-coupling reagent, uracil-TT+BF4–, for Sonogashira-type reaction to install an alkyne functionality selectively at position C-5 of uracils. A series of terminal alkynes were tolerated well, affording the desired products in good to excellent yields. Moreover, mild conditions, low catalyst loading, a broad substrate scope, and excellent functional group tolerance are some notable features of the current protocol. Furthermore, byproduct thianthrene (TT) formed in this reaction has been recovered and reused for making the uracil-TT+ reagent, highlighting the sustainability of the method.

item.title: Selective Synthesis of Fused N -Heterocycles or Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons via Tunable Mono or Double Carbene Insertion of Indazoles with Diazo Compounds
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we disclose two distinct switchable reaction patterns of 3-aryl-1H-indazole with diazo arylidene succinimide. Under condition A, C–H-activation-initiated C–C/C–N bond formation via mono carbene insertion furnishes a fused N-heterocycle (indazolo[3,2-a]isoquinoline). Under condition B, C–H-activation-initiated triple C–C bond formation through double carbene insertion affords a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (benzo[g]chrysene). To our knowledge, this is the first selective synthesis of these two valuable products from the same substrates. Interestingly, the benzo[g]chrysene derivatives thus obtained displayed bright fluorescence properties owing to the π-conjugation skeletons, suggesting their potential imaging and tracking capacity.

item.title: Cu-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of (Hetero)Aryl Halides with Malonates: One-Pot Assembly of α-Arylacetic Acid Scaffolds
item.description:
Abstract
A direct synthesis of α-arylacetic acids from (hetero)aryl chlorides and bromides and malonates via Cu/oxalamide-catalyzed cross-coupling with tandem hydrolysis and decarboxylation is described. Enabled by tailored oxalamide ligand L4, the reaction proceeds smoothly under mild conditions with low catalyst loadings, exhibits a broad substrate scope, and can be scaled to the gram scale and applied in the late-stage modification of complex drug intermediates. Systematic evaluation of the steric and electronic properties of oxalamide ligands, combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations, elucidates that the ortho-sp2-hybridized nitrogen atom on the ligand is indispensable for catalytic activity. The nitrogen atom coordinates with the sodium cation in the oxidative addition transition state (TS-OA-1a), stabilizing the transition state and lowering the activation barrier through favorable noncovalent interaction.

item.title: Radical Fluoroalkoxylation of α-Mono/Trihalo Ketones
item.description:
Abstract
Herein we report a photocatalytic radical fluoroalkoxylation of α-mono/trihalo ketones via selective C–X (X = F, Cl, Br) bond activation. The protocol affords diverse α,α-difluoromonofluoromethoxy ketones from readily available α-halo ketones under mild conditions with broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. It is amenable to one-pot synthesis and late-stage diversification of pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules. The strategy is further applicable to trifluoroethoxylation and alkoxylation, demonstrating the versatility of this radical fluoroalkoxylation platform. Mechanistic studies, including EPR and radical-trapping experiments, support an O-centered radical pathway.

item.title: Reaction of α-Iodoalkyldifluoroboranes with Copper(II) Carboxylates via a Tetracoordinate Boron Intermediate
item.description:
Abstract
The reaction of α-iodoalkyldifluoroboranes with copper(II) carboxylates affords α-acyloxyalkyldifluoroboranes. In this process, the high Lewis acidity of alkyldifluoroboranes constitutes the driving force for the formation of a tetracoordinate boron intermediate, as suggested by 11B NMR spectroscopy analysis, which is an important intermediate in the formation of the desired products.

item.title: Identification and Cyclization Mechanism of Fungal (+)-β-Chamigrene Synthase
item.description:
Abstract
Chamigranes are a unique class of sesquiterpenoids featuring a spiro[5.5]undecane framework, yet their biosynthesis in fungi has remained elusive for decades. In this study, we identify and characterize ChamTS, a sesquiterpene synthase from the basidiomycetous fungus Cerrena albocinnamomea, which specifically catalyzes the formation of (+)-β-chamigrane. In vitro isotope-labeling experiments unveiled the cyclization pathway of ChamTS, revealing an initial 1,6-cyclization followed by a 1,5-proton shift and spirocycle-forming rearrangement. This work provides a foundation for the biosynthetic production and further engineering of β-chamigrane-type terpenoids.

item.title: Asymmetric Nickel-Catalyzed Hydroalkylation of Secondary Amide-Derived Enamides with α-Halo Boronic Esters: Access to Enantioenriched β-Aminoboronic Esters
item.description:
Abstract
A nickel-catalyzed enantioselective reductive hydroalkylation of secondary amide-derived enamides with α-halo boronic esters is described. This mild protocol delivers N–H amide-containing chiral β-aminoboronic esters in high yields and with excellent enantioselectivities. The reaction exhibits broad functional-group tolerance, and the products can be easily transformed into valuable chiral oxazolines and other derivatives, underscoring their synthetic utility.

item.title: Visible-Light-Induced Aziridination of Unactivated Alkenes via Energy-Transfer Cleavage of Sulfilimines
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report that the aziridination of alkenes proceeds via visible-light-mediated energy-transfer-induced cleavage of N-sulfonyl sulfilimines, which serve as bench-stable nitrene precursors with a recoverable dibenzothiophene moiety. This strategy proves to be efficient, delivering good to excellent yields for mono- to tetrasubstituted unactivated alkenes and styrenes, with its applicability further extended to pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies support an energy-transfer pathway involving a free triplet nitrene intermediate.

item.title: Electrochemical Oxidation of the Benzyl Position To Form Ketones or Aldehyde Using ZnCoMnO Electrodes
item.description:
Abstract
The oxidation of the benzyl position to a ketone and aldehyde demonstrates precise control over kinetic selectivity. In this study, we propose the use of a Zn0.2Co0.2Mn0.6O chemically modified electrode to achieve this oxidation. This approach utilizes an aqueous sodium chloride solution and ethanol or tetrahydrofuran as the electrolyte and solvent, respectively, and exhibits good tolerance toward various functional groups. Operating at a current density of 100 mA/cm2 with straightforward post-treatment procedures, the method shows promise for industrial-scale production. A series of control experiments has been conducted to propose a plausible reaction mechanism.

item.title: Lights, Molecule, Action: 3-(Diarylmethylene)isobenzofuranones as Heteroatom-Containing, Tunable Aggregation-Induced Emission Luminogens
item.description:
Abstract
New aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) featuring the 3-(diarylmethylene)isobenzofuranone scaffold are reported herein. This structural motif stands out as a heteroatom-containing, accessible, and tunable material. The origin of its AIE properties was studied, offering some mechanistic insights. The application of these AIEgens in pH sensing and cell imaging was also demonstrated.

item.title: Direct Pyridine Dearomatization via Organocatalytic Enantioselective [4 + 2] Cycloaddition Accessing Polyfused Aza-[2.2.2] Scaffolds
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report the first chiral phosphoric-acid-catalyzed asymmetric [4 + 2] dearomatization of monocyclic pyridines. Distinct from previous activation modes, this transformation proceeds under purely thermal conditions and does not require external irradiation or photoredox catalysis. Readily accessible nicotinic acid derivatives undergo efficient intramolecular [4 + 2] cycloaddition to furnish polyfused aza-bicyclo[2.2.2]octane frameworks with high levels of enantiocontrol. This work addresses the longstanding challenge associated with the functionalization of monocyclic pyridines and represents the first example of an asymmetric [4 + 2]-cycloaddition-based dearomatization of pyridines.

item.title: Nucleophile-Directed Dichloromethane-Mediated Coupling of Carboxylic Acids for Access to Acyl Hydrazides and 3-Amino-1,2,4-Oxadiazoles
item.description:
Abstract
Carboxylic acids undergo direct coupling with hydrazine using CH2Cl2 as the coupling reagent and K3PO4 as the base to afford acyl hydrazides. Conversely, sequential one-pot coupling with guanidine in the presence of Cs2CO3, followed by PIDA-mediated oxidative cyclization, delivers 3-amino-1,2,4-oxadiazoles. Both protocols tolerate diverse functional groups, and the oxadiazole synthesis enables late-stage derivatization of probenecid, adapalene, and ataluren. Control experiments suggest that hydrazine reacts primarily through a bis(acyloxy)methane intermediate, whereas guanidine can engage both bis(acyloxy)methane and acyloxymethyl chloride intermediates. These results demonstrate that CH2Cl2-mediated carboxylic acid activation constitutes a programmable coupling platform wherein the identity of the nitrogen nucleophile governs the reaction pathway.

item.title: [Graphical abstract added] Heteroarylation of Functionalized Alkenes via Hexafluoroisopropanol-Assisted Redox Activation of Areneazo-2-(2-nitro)propanes
Dynamic Clipping Synthesis of Rotaxanes via Siliconate-Forming Reaction from Bis-Catechol, Organotrimethoxysilanes, and Secondary Amines
item.description:
Abstract
This study presents the dynamic clipping synthesis of [2]rotaxanes composed of catechol siliconate ion–containing crown ethers and secondary ammonium ions. These interlocked structures are stabilized through ion–ion interactions and hydrogen bonding. The σ-symmetric rotaxane structure was elucidated via X-ray crystallography and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

item.title: Ring Expansion of Benzothiaselenazole-1-oxides via Five-Membered Selenonium Ion-Mediated Alkene Insertion into Se–N Bonds
item.description:
Abstract
Ring expansion of heterocyclic frameworks provides an efficient approach to structurally diverse bioactive molecules, yet such transformations of organoselenium heterocycles remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a calcium-catalyzed insertion of alkenes into the Se–N bonds of benzothiaselenazole-1-oxides, enabling modular ring expansion of these selenium-containing heterocycles. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support the involvement of an unprecedented five-membered selenonium ion intermediate that governs the regio- and site-selectivity. The reaction accommodates diverse 1,3-dienes and benzothiaselenazole-1-oxides, affording ring-expanded products in high efficiency with exclusive E-selectivity. Late-stage functionalization of natural products and drug molecules further demonstrates the synthetic utility of this method for the diversification of organoselenium scaffolds.

item.title: Polarity-Matched Formal [1 + 4] Annulation of Fluoroalkyl Hydrazonoyl Halides with α-Halo Hydrazone-Derived Azoalkenes
item.description:
Abstract
Fluoroalkyl hydrazonoyl halides are typically used as nitrile–imine 1,3-dipole precursors, whereas their carbon-centered reactivity remains underdeveloped. Herein we report a base-promoted formal [1 + 4] annulation of α-halo acylhydrazone-derived azoalkenes with fluoroalkyl hydrazonoyl halides, providing CF2H- and CF3-substituted pyrazolines. Control experiments, time-course NMR, Fukui function/dual-descriptor analysis, and DFT calculations support a stepwise polarity-matched C–C bond-forming/cyclization pathway.

item.title: Condition-Controlled Chemoselectivity Switching of Spiro-Epoxy Oxindoles: Access to Spiro-Oxetane Oxindoles
item.description:
Abstract
A condition-controlled switch in chemoselectivity has been achieved in the reaction of spiro-epoxy oxindoles with sulfur ylides. In contrast to the previously observed cyclopropanation pathway, Lewis acid catalysis with tert-BuOK in tert-BuOH at elevated temperature redirects the reaction toward a Corey–Chaykovsky-type ring expansion, affording spiro-2′-oxetane oxindoles in good yields. This transformation provides direct access to oxindoles bearing a strained four-membered oxetane ring at the C3 position, a spirocyclic motif of growing interest in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Ultrafast Mechanochemical Epoxidation of Aldehydes and Ketones
item.description:
Abstract
We report a mechanochemical Corey–Chaykovsky epoxidation that converts aldehydes and ketones to epoxides within minutes under an ambient atmosphere using sulfonium or sulfoxonium salts, KOH, and minimal liquid additives. The method accommodates a broad substrate scope, is readily scalable, and often enables simple extraction without chromatography. It further enables telescoped sulfonium generation–oxidation–epoxidation, tunable enone chemoselectivity, and direct conversion of imines to unstabilized aziridines. An unexpected dependence of reactivity on the ylide precursor halide reveals distinct mechanochemical reactivity from that under conventional solution-phase conditions.

item.title: Intramolecular [4 + 2] Cycloaddition via Photoredox Dual Dearomatization of Indole and Furan Units
item.description:
Abstract
Despite significant advances in the field of dearomatization, dual dearomatization remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report an intramolecular dual dearomatization reaction of indoles and furans by photoredox catalysis. This method enables the construction of four fused rings in a single step with exceptional regio- and diastereoselectivities under mild conditions. The products can be converted into furan-fused polycyclic scaffolds in a one-pot procedure by using p-toluenesulfonic acid. The synthetic utility of this approach was demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis and several downstream transformations. Mechanistic studies revealed that this reaction proceeds via a single-electron transfer (SET) pathway rather than an energy transfer pathway.

item.title: Photocatalytic Approach to Decarboxylative Amidation of Aryl Glyoxylic Acids with Hydrazines
item.description:
Abstract
A photocatalytic decarboxylative amidation methodology turns out to be a straightforward, sustainable, effective, mild, and metal-free protocol for the synthesis of amides. Here, we report a metal-free, environmentally friendly approach to the synthesis of amides via decarboxylative amidation of eco-friendly aryl glyoxylic acids with readily available hydrazines through C–N coupling using eosin Y as a photocatalyst, a CH3CN/H2O mixture as a green solvent, visible light as a renewable energy source, and air as an oxidant. More importantly, this approach exhibits a broad substrate scope, enabling the efficient conversion of diverse aryl glyoxylic acids and hydrazines into the desired products. Overall, this strategy establishes an excellent eco-friendly approach for the synthesis of biological drugs.

item.title: Catalytic Deamino-Diels–Alder and Formal [2+2+2] Annulation Enabled by Indolyl-Vinyl-Iminium as a C4 Synthon: Divergent Assembly of Indole Polycyclic Skeletons
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report indolyl-vinyl-iminium as a new C4 synthon. It enables the divergent assembly of indole polycyclic skeletons via cascade cyclizations, including a gold(I)-catalyzed intramolecular deamino-Diels–Alder reaction for the construction of benzo[b]carbazoles and a sequential gold(I)/HNTf2-catalyzed intermolecular formal [2+2+2] annulation that affords a broad spectrum of hexahydroindolo[2,3-b]carbazole derivatives. Theoretical calculations and control experiments shed light on the reaction mechanism and the origin of the diastereoselectivity.

item.title: Synthesis of Benzo[ b ]azepines via Intramolecular Cyclization of 2-Alkenyl- N -propargylanilines
item.description:
Abstract
An atom-economical and catalyst-free synthesis of benzo[b]azepines is described by tuning an intramolecular cyclization of 2-alkenyl-N-propargylanilines. The reaction was presumed to proceed through an in situ formation of aza-o-quinone methide (aza-o-QM), followed by 1,6-enyne cyclization under thermal conditions. The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope upon validation of various alkynes, arenes, and amine components. The experimental and DFT studies provide mechanistic support for the proposed transformation and insights into the reaction pathway.

item.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Atropisomeric 3,3′-Biindoles via Three-Component de Novo Indolization
item.description:
Abstract
The catalytic atroposelective synthesis of 3,3′-biindoles remains a formidable challenge due to the inherent configurational lability of the [5–5] heterobiaryl system. Herein, we report a three-component de novo indolization from simple α-keto aldehydes, 2-substituted indoles, and 2-naphthylamines, enabled by a relay catalysis of Ca(NTf2)2 and chiral phosphoric acid. This cascade constructs both the biindole framework and the chiral axis in one operation, tolerating a broad range of substituents to afford diverse products with good yields and excellent enantioselectivities.

item.title: HBr-Catalyzed Construction of Sulfur-Containing Heterocycles via Difunctionalization of Alkenes
item.description:
Abstract
Sulfur-containing heterocycles are important chemical entities and key structural motifs in many biologically active molecules, representing valuable but synthetically challenging building blocks. Herein, we report a new method for the construction of sulfur-containing heterocycles under mild conditions using a green oxidative system composed of HBr and DMSO. This transformation employs inexpensive and readily available thiophenols as the sulfur source, operates without external photocatalysts and metals, and offers a general approach for the construction of small-ring and bridged-ring systems.

item.title: Photocatalytic 1,4-Phosphonocarboxylation of 1,3-Enynes with CO 2 : Synthesis of Tetrasubstituted Phosphorus-Containing Allenic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a visible-light photoredox-catalyzed Phosphonocarboxylation of 1,3-enynes with diarylphosphine oxides and CO2, utilizing a cost-effective photosensitizer under transition-metal-free and base-free conditions. This reaction enables the highly regioselective synthesis of a diverse range of tetra-substituted allenoic acids bearing phosphoryl group. Characterized by broad substrate scope, excellent regio-/chemoselectivity and facile scalability, it provides a practical platform for the construction of functionalized allenes with great potential for further derivatization.

item.title: Rhodium-Catalyzed Three-Component C(sp 3 )–H Activation of 8-Methyl Quinolines with Diazo Compounds and Formaldehyde/Formaldimine to Access Dual C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Bonds
item.description:
Abstract
The development of transition-metal-catalyzed three-component C(sp3)–H activation represents one of the most efficient strategies for the rapid construction of complex molecular architectures. Particularly, leveraging this strategy for the direct formation of dual C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds offers distinct advantages, whereas it remains largely challenging and underdeveloped. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed three-component C(sp3)–H activation of 8-methyl quinolines with diazo compounds and formaldehyde/formaldimine. This protocol not only provides a novel route for the construction of dual C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds via a 1,1-addition process but also offers a convenient pathway to access a diverse array of 8-alkyl quinoline derivatives under mild conditions.

item.title: Chiral Boron Complex-Catalyzed Asymmetric [2π+2σ] Cycloaddition of β-Fluoroalkyl-α,β-Unsaturated Ketones with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
item.description:
Abstract
Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs), three-dimensional benzene bioisosteres characterized by high sp3 carbon content, hold great promise for diverse applications in medicinal chemistry. While racemic BCH synthesis has advanced significantly, highly enantioselective approaches are still comparatively scarce. Here, we report an enantioselective [2π+2σ] cycloaddition of β-fluoroalkyl-α,β-unsaturated ketones with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) catalyzed by a chiral (R)-3,3′-(3,5-(CF3)2-C6H3)2-BINOL–boron complex. This approach overcomes major limitations of existing metal-catalyzed and photochemical methods. This transformation provides BCH derivatives featuring CF3- or C2F5-bearing stereocenters in moderate to high yields with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to >20:1 dr and >99% ee). This mild catalytic protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope and enables the rapid construction of complex fluoroalkyl-containing BCH scaffolds.

item.title: Synthesis of Axially and Centrally Chiral Alkylidenecyclobutanes Enabled by Catalytic Enantioselective Allylboration
item.description:
Abstract
A chiral phosphoric acid catalyzes asymmetric allylboration of stereodefined alkenylcyclobutyl boronates with aldehydes, constructing alcohol-functionalized alkylidenecyclobutanes (ACBs) bearing both axial and central chirality. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions with broad scope, affording products in high yields with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to >20:1 dr, 99% ee). Combining substrate stereocontrol with a Mitsunobu inversion allows selective switching of all three stereogenic centers of the ACBs using a single catalyst system. Utility is showcased by stereoselective syntheses of spiro[2.3]hexane and oxa-spiro[2.3]hexane bearing multiple stereocenters.

item.title: Dihydrobenzofuran Formation through Ring Contraction of Dihydroisocoumarin Synthesized by a Polyketide Synthase Assembly Line with a Terminal Reductase Domain in Asperfuran Biosynthesis
item.description:
Abstract
Asperfuran is an antifungal natural product with a dihydrobenzofuran (DHB) nucleus. Herein, we identify a biosynthetic gene cluster responsible for its biosynthesis from Neosartorya pseudofischeri. Genetic and biochemical analysis revealed that the DHB nucleus of asperfuran is formed by a flavin-dependent monooxygenase-catalyzed ring contraction of a dihydroisocoumarin precursor, which is generated by a collaborative polyketide synthase assembly line with a C-terminal reductase domain. Our work unraveled a novel biosynthetic route to DHB synthesis.

item.title: Visible-Light-Mediated Tandem Heck-Type Arylation/[4+2] Electrocyclization Process to Access 9,10-Dihydronaphthalene
item.description:
Abstract
Given their biological and synthetic importance, the construction of 9,10-dihydronaphthalene scaffolds is a pivotal transformation in organic synthesis, serving as a gateway to various bioactive natural products and functional materials. Herein, we develop a visible-light-driven, EDA-mediated Heck-type arylation/[4+2] electrocyclization tandem process, enabling the facile assembly of 9,10-dihydronaphthalene compounds by starting from readily available feedstock chemicals. A range of cinnamate and iodobenzene compounds showed good compatibility with this reaction system. The rationally designed reaction sequence exemplifies a telescoped route for the rapid construction of a multicyclic system with high reaction efficiency.

item.title: Tapping Water as an Oxygen Source: Visible-Light-Driven Synthesis of 4 H -Pyrans from 5-Alkynyl Ketones and Sulfonyl Chlorides
item.description:
Abstract
4H-Pyrans are privileged bioactive scaffolds, yet their oxygen is invariably sourced intramolecularly from carbonyl derivatives, restricting structural diversity accessible through established paradigms. Herein, we report a visible light-driven strategy that repurposes water as an extrinsic oxygen source to enable divergent access to two classes of tetrasubstituted 4H-pyrans from readily available 5-alkynyl ketones and sulfonyl chlorides. Using inexpensive 4CzIPN, this protocol delivers over 40 examples in up to 72% yield. Mechanistic studies (X-ray corroborated) reveal photoinduced water-mediated oxysulfonylation of unactivated alkynes as the pivotal branching step. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through late-stage functionalization, gram-scale operation, and facile conversion to structurally diverse 6- and 7-membered heterocycles.

item.title: Aminohalogenation of Alkenes Enabled by I(I)/I(III) Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
An iodoarene-catalyzed aminohalogenation of alkenes is reported via an I(I)/I(III) catalytic cycle. This protocol enables the unified installation of Cl, Br, and I across diverse alkenes at room temperature, employing inexpensive halogen sources. Notably, aryl- and alkyl-substituted alkenes exhibit divergent regioselectivities, which are dictated by the interplay of steric and electronic effects, manifested as Markovnikov selectivity for aryl alkenes and sterically controlled attack for alkyl alkenes. Mechanistic studies support an electrophilic pathway involving a hypervalent imidoiodine intermediate.

item.title: Conformational Locking Enables Chemoselective Direct 2-Deoxyglycosylation of C-4 Equatorial Glycals under Bi-Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
We demonstrate the chemoselective 2-deoxyglycosylation of formidable C-4 equatorial glycals enabled by a conformationally constrained protecting-group strategy. A proof-of-principle for the Bi(OTf)3-mediated 2-deoxyglycosylation of trans-fused 3,4-O-TIPDS-protected l-rhamnal, d-glucal, and d-xylal is illustrated using carbohydrates, amino-acids, and bioactive-natural products, providing structurally diverse 2-deoxy and 2,6-dideoxyglycoconjugates. Mechanistic insights into the distinctive structures of the glycosyl species revealed that conformational locking restricts the accessible 5H4 glycal and 4H3 oxocarbenium ion conformations, thereby favoring 1,2-addition and circumventing the Ferrier pathway.

item.title: Water-Phase Synthesis of 2,5-Methanobenzo[ d ][1,3,6]oxadiazocine with Low Catalyst Loading
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a novel strategy to construct bridged benzo[1,3,6]oxadiazocine scaffold from γ-hydroxy enals and o-phenylenediamine, a transformation that diverges from the conventional benzimidazole formation via aldehyde 1,2-addition. This protocol features unprecedented reactivity, green conditions (water solvent, 1 mol % catalyst, room temperature), simple operations, broad substrate scope, and versatile product derivatization, providing a practical and sustainable route to three-dimensional scaffolds of potential value in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Lanostane Triterpenoids from Kadsura coccinea : Four New Carbon Frameworks and Distinct Hsp90 Binding Modes
item.description:
Abstract
Twenty new lanostane triterpenoids, kadsuracoccinins A–T (1–20, respectively), were isolated from the stems of Kadsura coccinea, with compounds 1–7 constituting four new carbon scaffolds elucidated by NMR analysis, X-ray diffraction, GEMSTONE-NOE-aided fc-rDG/DDD, and ECD calculations. Luciferase-refolding, NMR STD, and SPR assays revealed compounds 4 and 8–10 as the first lanostane-type Hsp90 inhibitors, which bind Hsp90 through non-N-terminal modes, with compound 8 exhibiting a KD of 4.04 μM.

item.title: Tandem Rearrangement and Acyl Transfer of N -Naphthylhydroxyl-amines with Amides to Access ortho -Amidinated Naphthol Esters
item.description:
Abstract
A metal- and oxidant-free synthesis of ortho-amidinated naphthol esters from readily available N-naphthylhydroxylamines and amides has been developed using fluorosulfuryl imidazolium triflate under mild conditions. This transformation provides a broad range of products in good yields with excellent ortho selectivity and broad functional group tolerance. A scale-up experiment further demonstrates the practicality of the protocol. Notably, this tandem process enables concurrent C1 esterification and ortho amidination of the naphthalene framework, providing an efficient strategy for the difunctionalization of naphthalene derivatives. The densely functionalized products obtained through this method may serve as useful building blocks in medicinal chemistry and organic synthesis.

item.title: P III -Chelation-Enabled Ni(0)-Catalyzed Alkenylation of Nonacidic C–H in Biarylphosphines with Alkynes
item.description:
Abstract
A P(III)-chelation-assisted Ni(0)-catalyzed C–H alkenylation of biarylphosphines with alkynes is reported, enabling the functionalization of nonacidic arene C–H bonds without a stoichiometric base. The protocol accommodates a broad range of biarylphosphines and alkynes, affording diversely alkenylated biaryl monophosphines in up to 94% yield. Mechanistic studies confirm irreversible C–H cleavage as the rate-determining step. This work provides a sustainable and cost-effective alternative to precious-metal-based methods for the late-stage diversification of biaryl phosphine ligands.

item.title: Rh(III)-Catalyzed Sequential Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cycloadditions toward Functionalized Indeno[1,2- c ]isoquinolines
item.description:
Abstract
The development of transient directing groups that are generated and erased in situ has created new opportunities for catalytic C–H functionalization. This study reported a Rh(III)-catalyzed cascade annulation of readily available amidinium salts 1 or ethyl benzimidates 2 with 2-diazoindane-1,3-diones 3, providing functionalized indeno[1,2-c]isoquinolines (IIQLs) 6 and 7. This transformation integrated C–H activation, carbene insertion, and intramolecular cyclization into a single catalytic sequence. The resulting products subsequently underwent a second Rh(III)-catalyzed [4 + 2] annulation with diarylalkynes 4 or 2-diazoketones 5, furnishing structurally complex pentacyclic frameworks 8. Mechanistic studies suggest that Lewis acid-promoted amino–imine tautomerization accompanied by double-bond migration generated a transient imine from the embedded 2-aminopyridine-type motif. This substrate-derived imine directed o-aryl C(sp2)–H activation and was subsequently erased, eliminating the need for the installation and removal of permanent directing groups as well as the use of external transient directing agents. Overall, this modular strategy enabled the efficient construction of densely fused heterocyclic architectures by combining indane-1,3-dione and isoquinoline scaffolds, providing a versatile platform for the synthesis of structurally sophisticated molecules with potential applications in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: Divergent Three-Component Assembly of Difluoromethyl 1,3,4-Oxadiazoles
item.description:
Abstract
A divergent three-component assembly strategy for the construction of difluoromethylated compounds is established. Using benzohydrazide, carbon disulfide and sodium chlorodifluoroacetate as reaction partners, two types of heterocyclic products, namely 3-difluoromethyl-1,3,4-oxadiazole-2-thiones and 2-difluoromethylthio-1,3,4-oxadiazoles, are efficiently afforded via this protocol. This reaction exhibits robust functional group compatibility; halogens, nitro groups, trifluoromethyl substituents as well as various heterocyclic skeletons are well tolerated, and the target products were obtained with satisfactory yields.

item.title: Photoredox/Cobalt-Catalyzed SO 2 -Retaining Truce–Smiles Rearrangement Induced by Hydrogen Atom Transfer (HAT)
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, a distinctive hydrogen atom transfer (HAT)-initiated SO2-retaining Truce–Smiles rearrangement of unactivated alkenes under dual photoredox and cobalt catalysis is disclosed. A diverse array of γ/δ-heteroarylalkyl sulfones are efficiently constructed in high yields via a one-step operation. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions with high efficiency and broad substrate generality, accommodating mono- and disubstituted terminal alkenes as well as di- and trisubstituted internal alkenes. Moreover, an unusual 1,6-aryl migration is proven to be feasible in the reaction.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Direct β-C(sp 3 )–H Hydroxylation of Aliphatic Amides with Aqueous H 2 O 2
item.description:
Abstract
Carbonyl-directed Pd(II)-catalyzed β-C(sp3)–H hydroxylation of aliphatic amides has been accomplished using H2O2 (30% aq.) as the oxidant. Promoted by 3-pyridinesulfonic acid, the transformation proceeds under mild conditions to furnish β-hydroxy amides that are important structural motifs in bioactive molecules. The oxidation accommodates diverse native amides, including secondary, tertiary, cyclic, and α-hydrogen-containing substrates. The use of environmentally benign H2O2 (30% aq.) as the oxidant improves the sustainability and practicality of the procedure. The substrate scope, functional group tolerance, monoselectivity, and postsynthetic modifications are important practical features.

item.title: Dehydroxylative Cross-Electrophile Couplings of 4-Hydroxypyridines with Disulfides for Pyridyl Thioether Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
An efficient dehydroxylative cross-electrophile coupling of 4-hydroxypyridines with disulfides by employing diphenylphosphine oxide as an activator was developed. The thiolative protocol proceeded effectively via the cleavage of a relatively inert C–OH bond to produce a wide plethora of pyridyl thioethers in moderate to excellent yields. The coupling protocol could also be scaled up with ease and successfully applied to the utilization of diselenide as a substrate. Mechanistic exploration disclosed that in situ-generated S-aryl diphenylphosphinothioate from the reaction of diaryl disulfide with diphenylphosphine oxide presumably functions as the pivotal intermediate of the thioetherification.

item.title: Regio- and Chemoselective 1,2-Reduction of Quinolines Mediated by Borane and a Base
item.description:
Abstract
Selective reduction of readily available quinolines has gained continuous interest in both academia and industry. Described herein is a simple borane (THF·BH3)-mediated 1,2-selective reduction of quinolines in the presence of a simple base under transition-metal-free conditions with high functional group tolerance. Furthermore, this method allows for the facile preparation of N-protected 1,2-dihydroquinolines from commercially available acyl chlorides. The experimental and theoretical studies reveal a reaction mechanism of selective reduction via an intermolecular process that contrasts with the intuitive expectation and traditional concepts. These investigations demonstrate that coordination of borane enables reactivity distinct from that observed in well-studied metal catalysis.

item.title: Polysubstituted Fluoroalkylalkene Formation through Photoredox/Copper Dual Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we have developed photoredox/copper dual catalysis for the synthesis of structurally useful polysubstituted fluoroalkylalkenes. The cascade reaction involves defluoronative difluoroalkyl radical formation, radical addition to vinylene carbonate, radical-metal binding, β-elimination, and decarboxylation. This approach efficiently affords stereoregular tri- and tetrasubstituted fluoroalkyl alkenes with broad functional group tolerance.

item.title: Heteroarylation of Functionalized Alkenes via Hexafluoroisopropanol-Assisted Redox Activation of Areneazo-2-(2-nitro)propanes
item.description:
Abstract
The hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP)-assisted thermal denitrogenative fragmentation of areneazo-2-(2-nitro)propanes enabled heteroarylation of functionalized alkenes through cooperative radical and redox processes. Bench-stable areneazo-2-(2-nitro)propanes served as versatile aryl radical precursors for carboheterocyclization with alkenyl esters, affording diverse arylated lactones and heterocycles with broad functional group tolerance. Mechanistically, the radical fragmentation–nitro–nitrite isomerization of areneazo-2-(2-nitro)propanes generated nitric oxide that underwent a redox process with tertiary radical intermediates to promote heterocyclization. The oxidant-free conditions generated dinitrogen and acetone as benign byproducts.

item.title: Photoredox-Enabled Difluoromethylation Cyclization and Quinoxalin-2(1 H )-one Integration: Access to gem -Difluoro-Quinolines
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, a novel protocol for the photoredox-enabled intramolecular difluoromethylation cyclization and intermolecular domino quinoxalin-2(1H)-one integration is established. This version allows facile access to structurally diverse gem-difluoro-quinolines. A wide substrate scope, wide functional group compatibility, bioactive molecule decoration, and gram-scale amplification attest to the utility of this protocol. A radical cyclization mechanism is proposed on the basis of radical inhibition experiments, a visible-light irradiation on–off test, AQE calculations, and Stern–Volmer fluorescence quenching experiments.

item.title: Direct C2 Acylation of Free ( N –H) Indoles Enabled by Pd(II)/Norbornene Cooperative Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
We report a regioselective C2 acylation of free (N–H) indoles enabled by Pd(II)/norbornene (NBE) cooperative catalysis. This protocol circumvents the pre-installation and removal of N-directing groups, enabling direct C2–H acylation under mild, open-air conditions. Utilizing acid anhydrides as acylating agents, the reaction shows good functional group tolerance and provides a highly step-economical platform to biologically relevant 2-acylindoles, as demonstrated by the streamlined, single-step synthesis of a platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) kinase inhibitor.

item.title: A Doubly Nitrogen-Bridged Chiral Spirobifluorene Dimeric Macrocycle: Synthesis, Properties, and Thermally Activated Electron Exchange in the Oxidized State
item.description:
Abstract
A doubly nitrogen-bridged chiral spirobifluorene dimer with a rigid double-helical structure was synthesized, and its one-electron oxidized species was investigated as a mixed-valence system. Variable-temperature ESR measurements revealed thermally activated intramolecular electron exchange with a very small activation enthalpy (ΔH‡ = 1.25 kcal mol–1), despite limited electronic communication across the doubly spiro-linked redox units.

item.title: Boereguasins A–D, Cytochalasins from Boeremia exigua with Differential MAPK/NF-κB Inhibition
item.description:
Abstract
Four unprecedented cytochalasins, boereguasins A–D (1–4, respectively), were purified from the endophytic fungus Boeremia exigua. Structurally, compound 1 contains an adenosine moiety and features a novel bridged 5/6/13/5/6/5 ring system. Compound 2 represents the first cytochalasin with an odd-numbered carbon chain (19 carbons), which is presumably assembled via the fungal polyketide synthase pathway from an unusual propionyl-CoA starter unit. Compound 3 incorporates an unusual 15-membered carbocyclic ring, while compound 4 possesses a novel 5/6/14/6 tetracyclic scaffold. The structures were established by comprehensive spectroscopic analysis, ECD calculations, and DP4+ analysis. Compound 2 exhibited potent anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-induced RAW264.7 macrophages, significantly reducing NO, TNF-α, IL-6, and PGE2 levels. It suppressed the MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway by inhibiting the phosphorylation of ERK, JNK, IκBα, and p65 and downregulating iNOS and COX-2 expression. Transcriptomic and docking studies confirmed that 2 targets key regulators and stably binds to the active pockets of TPL2 and NF-κB p65. In vivo, 1 and 2 reduced foot edema and inflammatory cytokines, with no acute toxicity observed.

item.title: Oxidative Fluorination of β-Ketoamides: Guanidinium Iodides as Iodoarene Alternatives
item.description:
Abstract
A guanidinium iodide-catalyzed oxidative fluorination of β-ketoamides enables umpolung α-fluorination, replacing iodoarenes with a simple iodide source. Using HF·pyridine as the fluoride source and mCPBA as the oxidant in dichloroethane, quaternary α-fluoro-β-ketoamides are obtained in up to 92% yields with a broad substrate scope, tolerating aromatic, aliphatic, and acyclic systems. Mechanistic studies identify hypoiodous and/or iodous acids as the catalytic species, while the guanidinium cation enhances both solubility and reactivity of the iodide.

item.title: A General Method to Prepare α,β-Dehydroamino Acid Esters from the Addition of β-Ketoesters to Nitrosobenzenes
item.description:
Abstract
α,β-Dehydroamino acids (ΔAAs) represent important structural motifs in natural products and synthetic peptides, and serve as versatile precursors for unnatural amino acids. This work demonstrates a mild, general, and efficient protocol for ΔAA synthesis via DBU-mediated addition of β-ketoesters to nitrosobenzenes. Notably, nucleophilic 3-benzoyllactones deliver lactone-bearing ΔAAs. Intriguingly, linear 2-arylmethyl 3-benzoyl esters afford (Z)-configured ΔAAs whereas other 2-alkyl 3-benzoyl esters produce (E)-ΔAAs. Mechanistic analysis validates a complex cascade process featuring a [1,3]-H-shift rearrangement.

item.title: Tandem Acylation/C–H Functionalization Cyclization to Access Indanone-Fused BODIPYs and Their NIR-Emissive α,α-Dimers with Deep LUMO Levels
item.description:
Abstract
Mono- and bis-indanone-fused BODIPYs are synthesized via tandem acylation and intramolecular C–H functionalization cyclization. This rigid fused-ring framework extends the π-conjugated system, affording red-shifted, intense absorption/emission and high quantum yields (>0.90). Regioselective FeCl3-mediated oxidative coupling yields the α,α-linked dimer, inducing a 216 nm redshift with emission maxima at 823 nm. Notably, the electron-withdrawing indanone units lower the LUMO to −4.10 eV and enable radical anions, an electronic property generally absent in conventional fused BODIPYs. Owing to their tunable absorption, bright emission, and good biocompatibility, these indanone-fused dyes enable high-contrast, multicolor lipid droplet (LD) imaging in living cells.

item.title: Halogen Sources for the Controlled Dihalotrifluoroethoxylation and Dihalogenation of Alkynylsilanes in a Trifluoroethanol Aqueous Solution
item.description:
Abstract
We herein report the diiodotrifluoroethoxylation of alkynylsilanes with NH4I in a trifluoroethanol aqueous solution under mild conditions. This method enables a multicomponent one-pot reaction of diverse trifluoroethoxy-functionalized diiodoalkenes with high regio- and stereoselectivity. In addition, the resulting vicinal diiodinates are valuable in late-stage skeletal editing and in the discovery of new fluorescence materials. Moreover, dibromination and dichlorination, as well as the reaction mechanism, have also been investigated.

item.title: Lewis Acid Catalyzed Solvent Switching Enabled Diastereodivergent Hydroimination of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
item.description:
Abstract
A Lewis acid catalyzed, solvent-switching diastereodivergent hydroimination of acyl bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with diphenylmethanimine is reported. Using a rhodium Lewis acid catalyst, the reaction proceeds with excellent and predictable diastereocontrol simply by changing the solvent: in toluene, the corresponding anti 1,3-disubstituted cyclobutanes are formed with >20:1 diastereomeric ratio (d.r.), whereas switching to HFIP reverses the diastereochemical outcome to deliver the syn products. Broad functional group tolerance is demonstrated across a range of aryl- and alkyl-substituted acylbicyclobutanes. Gram-scale reactions, product deprotection to free amines, and a practical sequence for imidazole auxiliary removal further highlight their synthetic utility.

item.title: Unlocking the Latent Dienophile Reactivity of Neutral Ketimines through Ketimine–Enamine Tautomerism: A Diastereoselective Povarov Reaction between Two Neutral Imines
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed Povarov reaction between two neutral imines enabled by the latent dienophile reactivity of ketimines. In situ-generated endocyclic enamines from benzo[b][1,4]oxazines undergo cycloaddition with aldimine-derived aza-dienes at room temperature, affording fused tetrahydroquinolines bearing a C4 quaternary stereocenter in good to excellent yields with complete diastereoselectivity. Aromatic and aliphatic aldimines are well tolerated. DFT studies support an inverse-electron-demand Diels–Alder mechanism, revealing an unusual reactivity paradigm enabled by ketimine-enamine tautomerism.

item.title: Preparation of Alkyl N -Alkylphosphonamidates by the Microwave-Assisted Selective Monoaminolysis of Dialkyl Phosphites
item.description:
Abstract
The title compounds, (RO)(NHR′)P(O)H, were synthesized earlier from P-chloro intermediates by substitutions or from dialkyl phosphites by reaction with organometallic reagents. Instead of these not clear-cut and not efficient transformations, a green, solvent- and catalyst-free synthesis of alkyl phosphonamidates has been developed by the microwave-assisted aminolysis of dialkyl phosphites. The monosubstitution was fully selective. Under more forcing conditions, an interesting side reaction was observed. The resulting products may be valuable reagents to prepare α-hydroxy- and α-aminophosphonic derivatives.

item.title: Modular Synthesis of Aerobactin–Aztreonam Conjugates with Enhanced Activity against Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae
item.description:
Abstract
A modular strategy enabled controlled mono- and difunctionalization of aerobactin and late-stage attachment of alkyne-bearing payloads by CuAAC. Application to aztreonam afforded the first aerobactin–antibiotic conjugates. Monovalent conjugate 3b showed superior activity against hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae KPN234 (MIC = 0.031 μM), a 16-fold improvement over aztreonam. Competition and iron-dependent activity studies supported aerobactin-pathway-dependent delivery, establishing aerobactin as a viable antibacterial delivery scaffold.

item.title: Crossing the Reactivity Threshold: Phosphonate-Directed, Gold-Catalyzed Oxygen Transfer to Alkynyl Phosphonates
item.description:
Abstract
The first gold-catalyzed oxygen-transfer reaction of alkynyl phosphonates is reported, providing regioselective access to oxazol-4-yl phosphonates through a formal (2+2+1) assembly. The low intrinsic reactivity of alkynyl phosphonates was overcome by pairing the weakly activating phosphonate group with a strongly π-acidic phosphite–gold(I) catalyst and an electronically attenuated O-transfer reagent. The synthetic value is underscored by a gram-scale synthesis, downstream elaborations to the phosphonic acids, and access to phosphonate analogues of bioactive oxazoles.

item.title: Noncovalent Interaction-Catalyzed High Conversion of Waste PET Plastics into Organic Esters under Mild Conditions
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a versatile esterolysis strategy, driven by noncovalent interactions (such as hydrogen bonding and electrostatic forces), that depolymerizes waste poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) into high-value molecular precursors under mild conditions. This strategy can be applied to a broad range of ester substrates, including carboxylates, carbonates, and silicon/titanium (Si/Ti)-based esters. A series of mechanistic studies reveal that the TBD catalyst serves a dual function. It catalyzes the in situ generation of methanol from dimethyl carbonate while simultaneously driving the cleavage of C–O bonds in PET via hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions. Ultimately, this work establishes a widely applicable and sustainable platform for PET upcycling, which not only enhances the valorization of plastic waste but also provides a scalable solution to the global plastic pollution crisis.

item.title: Biocatalytic Cascade from Geraniol to Enantiopure ( R )-Citronellal Using an Aryl-Alcohol Oxidase and Ene Reductase
item.description:
Abstract
(R)-Citronellal, a key intermediate for (−)-menthol and other valuable fragrance compounds, is traditionally synthesized by unsustainable chemical methods, with low selectivity. Herein, we report a one-pot enzymatic cascade converting geraniol to enantiopure (R)-citronellal using Streptomyces hiroshimensis aryl-alcohol oxidase ShAAO and ene reductase Saccharomyces cerevisiae OYE2_Y83V. A scale-up reaction at 100 mM geraniol produced 95 mg of (R)-citronellal with an enantiomeric excess of >99.8%, demonstrating a sustainable, preparative-scale, and highly selective route to chiral terpenoids.

item.title: Discovery of Diverse Polycyclic Polyprenylated Acylphloroglucinols from Hypericum kouytchense with Anti-Liver Fibrosis Potential
item.description:
Abstract
Hypercoretions A–C (1–3), three types of unprecedented polycyclic polyprenylated acylphloroglucinols (PPAPs), were isolated from Hypericum kouytchense using a combined FBMN and UV-guided isolation method. Notably, hypercoretion A (1) represents a unique nor-PPAP characterized by a rearranged 5/6/6/5 tetracyclic skeleton, while hypercoretion B (2) is the first example of a seco-nor-PPAP featuring an unusual 5/5/5 tricyclic skeleton. Their structures were established via spectroscopic analyses, X-ray diffraction, vibrational circular dichroism, and quantum chemical calculations. Biologically, the isolates were evaluated for their anti-liver fibrosis activities in TGF-β1-stimulated LX-2 hepatic stellate cells.

item.title: Sulfonylation of Cyclic Allylborates with DABSO: Synthesis of Allylic Sulfones Having an Allylic Boronate Moiety
item.description:
Abstract
A three-component coupling reaction for the synthesis of highly substituted allylic sulfones bearing an allylic boronate moiety is described. This method uses cyclic allylborates, a sulfur dioxide surrogate (DABSO), and organic halides such as alkyl halides and allylic bromides. The reaction proceeds with high α-selectivity, which is notable since γ-selective functionalization is more common for allylic boron compounds. The reaction demonstrates a broad substrate scope with respect to both the cyclic allylborates and organic halides. Mechanistic investigations suggest that the reaction proceeds via the initial formation of a γ-functionalized SO2 intermediate, followed by a rearrangement to afford the final α-product.

item.title: Highly Stereoselective α-Glycosylation by Acid–Base Catalysis with the Help of Two Additives: The Counterion of the Acid and a Heterocyclic Base
item.description:
Abstract
The stereoselective synthesis of 1,2-cis glycosides remains a longstanding challenge in carbohydrate chemistry. Herein, we report a cooperative acid–base catalysis strategy based on N-iodosuccinimide/triethylsilane and 8-nitroquinoline for highly α-selective glycosylation with O-glycosyl trichloroacetimidate donors. This catalytic system enables the synthesis of over 50 glycosides in good to excellent yields under mild conditions. The synthetic utility was further demonstrated through gram-scale reactions and the convergent synthesis of an α-(1→6)-linked hexasaccharide.

item.title: Rh(I)/Bisoxazolinephosphine-Catalyzed Regio- and Enantioselective Allylation of Indenes
item.description:
Abstract
A highly regio- and enantioselective synthesis of chiral 3-allyl-1H-indenes has been developed using a Rh(I)/bisoxazolinephosphine catalyst in combination with 4-dimethylaminopyridine (DMAP). The tridentate NPN* ligand binds tightly to Rh(I), effectively preventing catalyst deactivation by the indene products and enabling high yields with excellent stereocontrol. Mechanistic studies reveal an unconventional pathway involving initial formation of a 1,5-diene intermediate, followed by Rh/DMAP cocatalyzed 1,3-proton migration to yield the thermodynamically favored 1,4-diene products. The method exhibits broad functional group compatibility with both allylic carbonates and indene derivatives, affording the desired products in up to 98% yield, >99% ee, and >20:1 rr.

item.title: Synthesis of Bispidine–Isoxazolidine-Fused Multicyclic Scaffolds via Nitrone [3+2] Cycloaddition: Toward “Hetero-Lupine Alkaloids”
item.description:
Abstract
We present a highly efficient strategy for the assembly of bispidine–isoxazolidine-fused multicyclic structures via [3+2] cycloaddition of alkenes to a nitrone-functionalized bispidine framework. The reaction smoothly delivers diverse hybrid heterocycles featuring complex stereochemistry at the isoxazolidine–bispidine junction point in high yields and good selectivity. This approach opens a straightforward pathway to new synthetic analogues of natural compounds (primarily lupine alkaloids) and may prove to be useful for the discovery of new bioactive molecules and ligands for catalysis.

item.title: Whole-Cell LkADH-Catalyzed Asymmetric Reduction Enables Direct Access to Cyclohexylidene Axially Chiral Alcohols
item.description:
Abstract
Enantioenriched axially chiral alcohols are key building blocks for asymmetric synthesis and drug discovery, yet biocatalytic access to cyclohexylidene variants is rarely reported due to spatial separation between the hydroxyl site and chiral axis. Herein, engineered Lactobacillus kefir Alcohol Dehydrogenase (LkADH) whole-cell catalysts enable aqueous asymmetric reduction of cyclohexylidene ketones toward S-configured axially chiral alcohols. The L153K variant gave 94% conversion and 98:2 er for 2a; diverse aryl/heteroaryl substrates afforded products with high conversions and up to 99:1 er. The whole-cell strategy avoids enzyme purification and the addition of a separate purified GDH cofactor-recycling enzyme, facilitating practical synthesis verified by scale-up and downstream derivatization. This work develops a biocatalytic route and broadens the synthetic scope of LkADH reduction for uncommon axially chiral alcohols.

item.title: Access to Structurally Diverse 1-Boraphenalenes via the Nucleophilic Hydroboration Reaction
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a strategy for the synthesis of 1-boraphenalenes via the nucleophilic hydroboration of 8-alkynyl-1-lithionaphthalenes under mild reaction conditions. In contrast to previously reported electrophilic methods, the present protocol is compatible with silicon- and germanium-substituted substrates as well as a variety of Lewis basic functional groups, providing complementary access to structurally diverse 1-boraphenalenes that are difficult to obtain by conventional approaches.

item.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Strain-Release Alkyl–Alkyl Cross-Coupling of N -Chlorocyclopropamides with Tertiary α-Bromo Esters
item.description:
Abstract
We report a nickel-catalyzed alkyl–alkyl cross-electrophile coupling of N-chlorocyclopropamides with tertiary alkyl bromides. This method leverages cyclopropane strain release to generate alkyl radicals via β-scission of nitrogen-centered radicals, enabling efficient C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation under mild reductive conditions. The protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance, affording diverse aliphatic products in good to excellent yields. Mechanistic studies support a radical relay pathway driven by strain-release ring opening and nickel-mediated cross-coupling. This strategy provides a modular, practical approach to complex aliphatic frameworks, expanding the utility of strain-release chemistry in cross-electrophile coupling.

item.title: Strain-Release-Driven Ring Opening of Vinyl-Azabicyclobutanes: A Platform for Allylic Functionalization
item.description:
Abstract
A new class of azetidine-tethered allylic acetates was prepared via strain-release reactions of vinyl-ABB using acetic acid as nucleophile and used for Tsuji-Trost allylation. A broad range of primary and secondary alkylamines, sulfinates, active methylene compounds and azlactones were employed as nucleophiles to access tetrasubstituted alkylidene-azetidines in good yield. Also, in the absence of any nucleophile, acetate rearrangement was reported via the attack of the counter acetate anion from the less hindered site of the π-allyl-palladium species. Boc-deprotected tetrasubstituted alkylidene azetidine shows promising antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

item.title: Synthesis and Host–Guest Chemistry of Pyrene-Embedded Helical Carbon Nanohoops
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report the synthesis of pyrene-embedded carbon nanohoops (3PyCPP) via a triangular gold complex-templated assembly strategy, in which three pyrene units are strategically linked at their 1,6-positions. This synthetic approach yields four crystal structures, and only the enantiomeric conformers [(15,6)AAA3PyCPP and (15,6)BBB3PyCPP] are exclusively observed in the crystalline state. 3PyCPP demonstrates a moderate fluorescence quantum yield (ΦF = 46.2%) and a large Stokes shift. Moreover, host–guest chemistry studies reveal that 3PyCPP binds C70 in an inclusion manner to form a unique 1:1 complex. This work shows a type of carbon-rich nanohoop with tailored structures and dual utility in optoelectronics and supramolecular host–guest systems.

item.title: Remote Quaternary Stereocenter Construction toward Crinine-Type Alkaloids Via Chiral Organoiodine-Mediated Biomimetic Oxidative para -Dearomative C–C Coupling
item.description:
Abstract
Remote stereocontrol in iodine(III)-mediated oxidative phenol dearomatization is challenging because the C–C bond-forming site is distant from the chiral iodine environment. We designed ortho-brominated phenol substrates and a C2-symmetric organoiodine catalyst to enable biomimetic para-dearomative coupling. This strategy constructs remote all-carbon quaternary stereocenters through seven-membered-ring-forming oxidative C–C coupling, enabling total syntheses of (+)-oxomaritidine and (+)-oxovittatine and formal syntheses of (+)-maritidine and (+)-vittatine. The ortho-substituent effects on enantioselectivity suggest that substrate organization may contribute to remote asymmetric induction.

item.title: Divergent Total Synthesis of 17- nor -Excelsinidine and Geissoschizoline
item.description:
Abstract
Using the key intermediate previously established in our group’s synthetic investigations of monoterpenoid indole alkaloids, concise and efficient total synthetic routes toward the 17-nor-excelsinidine and geissoschizoline were developed. The synthesis of 17-nor-excelsinidine relied on oxidative cyclization and intramolecular N-alkylation as the pivotal transformations. Following this strategy, a concise total synthesis of this alkaloid was accomplished. For geissoschizoline, we developed a biomimetic synthetic route featuring a cascade reaction sequence: Mn(OAc)3-mediated oxidative cyclization and skeletal reorganization. The target molecule was secured in a seven-step longest linear sequence, alongside a formal synthesis of dehydrogeissoschizoline.

item.title: Sterically Congested 2,2-Dimethylphenylacetate Glycosyl Donors for Versatile Protecting-Group Manipulations and Orthogonal Glycosylations
item.description:
Abstract
We report glycosyl 2,2-dimethyl-2′-(4-methoxyphenylethynyl)phenylacetates (DMPA) as a new class of glycosyl donors featuring exceptional stability toward alcoholysis and broad compatibility with protecting-group manipulations. The sterically congested DMPA donors can be readily prepared through coupling with the corresponding acid or via late-stage installation of a reactive alkyne handle, providing a versatile platform for the construction of latent-active glycosyl donors. These donors are efficiently activated under NIS/TMSOTf conditions but remain dormant under Au(I) catalysis; notably, treatment with TMSOTf alone affords only a trace amount of product, which enables orthogonal one-pot glycosylation strategies. The combination of synthetic robustness, broad substrate scope, and protecting-group-manipulation compatibility provides a practical approach for the streamlined synthesis of complex oligosaccharides and glycoconjugates.
